from.place: The proof requires gluing equivariant module sections.

title: Gluing equivariant module sections
statement:
theorem equivariantModulePresheaf_isSheaf
    {V : Scheme.{u}} (ℓ : ℕ) {P : Type u} [Group P] [Finite P]
    (c : Scheme.GaloisCover (ULift.{u + 1} P) V)
    (N : Rep.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ) P) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf V.smallEtaleTopology (c.equivariantModulePresheaf ℓ N)

proof.text: Give the representation carrier the discrete topology. Form the type-valued presheaf H by precomposing Scheme.Etale.continuousMapSheaf on c.P with MorphismProperty.Over.pullback along c.π and forgetting abelian groups. Etale.isContinuous_overPullback and Functor.op_comp_isSheaf_of_isSheaf prove H is a sheaf. This reuses the existing library construction of the continuous-function sheaf instead of reconstructing pointwise gluing.

Define the private equivarianceSubfunctor of H by s(action(g,x)) = rho(g)(s(x)). The pullback universal property proves that sectionRestriction commutes with sectionAction, so the condition is stable under restrictions. Given a section locally in the subfunctor, compare s composed with action(g) with rho(g) composed with s. Both are continuous (the representation carrier is discrete), and restrictions agree by local equivariance and the commutation identity. Separatedness of H proves equality, so equivariance is local. Apply Mathlib Subfunctor.isSheaf_iff to obtain the sheaf condition for the equivariant continuous functions.

Construct the natural isomorphism from the underlying type presheaf of equivariantModulePresheaf to equivarianceSubfunctor.toFunctor. Its forward map turns locally constant functions into continuous functions and its inverse uses IsLocallyConstant.iff_continuous for the discrete carrier. Both inverses are pointwise identities; naturality follows from pullback.hom_ext identifying sectionRestriction with the base-change functor map. Transport the type-valued sheaf condition along this isomorphism. Reflect it through the module forgetful functor using explicit HasLimitsOfSize, PreservesLimitsOfSize and ReflectsLimitsOfSize instances. The coefficient ring ZMod ell has universe zero, so ModuleCat.hasLimitsOfSize uses universe arguments (u, u+1, u+1, 0).
